Interestingly, the secondary eclipse was not observed, suggesting the companion star may be significantly smaller or dimmer than the primary. The discovery passed rigorous vetting procedures, including pixel-level analysis and checks against existing catalogs of known variable stars, confirming this is a genuinely new find. This candidate represents the kind of stellar system that helps astronomers understand binary star properties and their orbital dynamics.

78955414.writeup: TIC 78955414 is a newly discovered eclipsing binary star system that completes one full orbit every 1.9967 days. When the primary star passes in front of its companion, the system dims by 3.17 percent - a dip detected with high confidence by automated search algorithms. Interestingly, no secondary eclipse was observed, suggesting the companion star may be significantly dimmer than its primary. This candidate had never appeared in any major variable-star catalog before, making it a genuine discovery. Additional observations confirmed the signal's authenticity, with the system passing all data-quality checks and showing a strong detection score from machine-learning analysis. TIC 78955414 offers astronomers a fresh target for understanding binary star systems.

86956236.writeup: Astronomers have discovered a new eclipsing binary star system called TIC 86956236, in which two stars orbit each other every 70.84 days. When the primary star passes in front of its companion, the system dims by about 5 percent - a dip significant enough to be detected from space-based observations. The discovery was made possible by analyzing data with advanced algorithms that identified subtle brightness changes in the star's light. This system does not appear in existing catalogs of known variable stars, making it a genuine new find. While a secondary eclipse from the companion star was not detected, multiple confirmation tests including detailed pixel-level analysis support that this is indeed a real eclipsing binary rather than a false signal or background object.
